correctness.rationale: Conditioned two-point polynomial integrals yield both moment identities for any acute, right or obtuse triangle. Inversion derives area, e2 and e3 with strictly positive area denominator, giving a uniquely determined cubic root multiset. A two-isosceles counterexample proves one moment insufficient. Fixed-product slack constraint is compact and connected; Lagrange multipliers reduce extrema to two isosceles candidates, whose difference is positive. The included checker performed exact rational integrations for six triangles and direct independent simulation. Finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The second moment is explicitly credited and not claimed as new. The retrieved full 2012 Bäsel work concerns invariant-line chords and interior point pairs, whereas the present fourth boundary-point moment, fixed-perimeter two-moment inverse, and sharp isosceles area envelope use a different endpoint measure and a specific new implication. value.rationale: The exact fourth moment, used alongside known m2 and measured perimeter, completes a globally valid and minimal finite-moment triangle reconstruction. At prescribed perimeter and area it supplies a complete nontrivial range and classifies two noncongruent isosceles extremizers. This distinguishes shapes that a second-moment measurement cannot, without claiming a noise-robust estimator or paper-sized general theory.
